summary: Separate the grammar imperatives from the 24/135 quotation
before: mawḏǝ́ʕ; moḏáʕ; 730;  iḏa d-oṯe d-məsniqitu l-mede ḥreno, ayko d-huwetu moḏéʕəl-li!
after: iḏa d-oṯe d-məsniqitu l-mede ḥreno, ayko d-huwetu moḏéʕəl-li!

replacement_examples.turoyo: iḏa d-oṯe d-məsniqitu l-mede ḥreno, ayko d-huwetu moḏéʕəl-li!
replacement_examples.translation: Wenn ihr noch etwas mehr braucht, so laßt es mich wissen, wo ihr auch seid!

rationale: The turoyo field fuses two standalone imperative forms and their grammar-page reference with a translated corpus example. Split them into two records in the same box. Retain 24/135 for the sentence: its supplied verse contains the sentence, despite the automatic not-found result.

The supplied 24/305 reads “u huḏoyawo”, with ḏ, not emphatic ḍ. Other glossary quotations from the same story consistently use huḏoyo (e.g. kly III, 24/300). This is a consonant error, not the permitted d/ḏ normalization.
The supplied JL 9.9/11 reads “kətlan rawmo rabṯo”. The same passage under ylf I also has rawmo. The w and m were transposed in this entry.
